title: Assistive overhaul: partial implementation
summary: This canvas retains the October 7 geometry as an explicitly historical route snapshot. The draft assistive implementation now records caller-reported task checks and can compare bounded declared source paths, explicitly named shared interfaces and common build controls without rescanning every source or dispatching a reviewer. Unchanged scoped bytes are partial applicability, not full dependency closure or passing test proof. A mixed old/new engine fixture checks byte-preserving upgrade, retained user stops, exact journal replay and older-client fail-closed behavior. Pending-prompt, full dependency, installed-host and release qualification remain incomplete. The historical approval arrows are not the current default. No release or installed-host qualification is implied.

changes.summary: The source-bound artifact guidance now explains optional shared input paths, targeted affected-check refresh, and explicit unassessed fallback. It also documents old-client refusal after modern schema writes and exact-operation forward recovery, not automatic downgrade. This still allows applicable in-scope work to proceed without approval codes or blanket reviewer redispatch.
The drafting owner now describes explicit shared_inputs for known common interfaces and configuration, with no invented dependency graph or extra artifact approval.

The pinned native bridge enables task-context as a bounded informational read and does not require future reviewer/approval producers simply to author a structurally valid draft. Installed host qualification is separate. Native Pi writer admission does not establish a complete live Pi workflow.

A new explicit batch review can select a passing rerun of still-reviewed work without replacing the original task review. The selected run must match its own recorded workspace; changed source or supporting evidence still requires reassessment.
The user-facing route table now points feature and sprint work at useful planned execution rather than per-task reviewer chains; real destructive actions still use their owning host/commit controls.
The skill index now labels brainstorming, planning, execution and optional reviewers as assistive instead of mandatory approval and double-review stages.
The sprint caller performs an index-first recorded-intent read, preserves actual owner decisions and ADR conflicts, then proceeds with authorized work without a second artifact approval system.
The sprint entry now routes to the assistive implementation body instead of requiring a fresh user approval and two reviews per task.
The feature entry now resumes a maintained spec/plan and task progress without another artifact certification prompt; independent commit and test controls remain.
Source refinement respects recorded deferrals and accepted ADR conflicts without turning each ordinary method adjustment into a separate authorization interview.
Attended feature execution now treats checkpoints as progress groups, not compulsory approval stops; it forwards real failures and continues independent work.
The implementation owner uses bounded task/source applicability for targeted rechecks, never treating scoped hash matches or caller notes as an independent review or full graph proof.
The test-first discipline now consumes the selected spec and actual relevant checks without requiring an extra artifact approval or context-delivery receipt.
The commit owner retains actual user commit permission, staged diff inspection, secrets and focused tests without requiring an artifact-specific acceptance receipt to stage.
PR preparation now reports unfinished implementation and verification honestly while retaining Git, merge ancestry and exact-head hosted CI controls.
Read-only task-context reassesses the bounded source subset and reports scoped_changed, scoped_unchanged or unassessed with scope_complete false; relevant changes guide targeted retests.

An unanswered legacy reconciliation can be superseded only when registered route and pending state agree and no durable attempt exists; macOS system parent aliases are canonicalized while symlinked selected repository roots remain forbidden. In-flight operations retain exact replay.
The old CLI helper has a reason-bound --supersede mode to retire only unanswered prompt routing. A committed or unknown mutation outcome retains its exact --recover path.

Task-check observations now retain directly referenced criterion identity and an optional bounded source-input fingerprint or an explicit unassessed reason, without executing tests or minting approval receipts.
Historical check observations keep whole-spec applicability while new ones bind only referenced criterion definitions, avoiding irrelevant spec changes without falsely claiming verified work.
Exact and batch symbol retrieval exposes reported check history under existing response budgets, without a snapshot or approval ticket.
Human HTML presents reported command checks in an escaped, explicitly unverified section; implementation state and source validation remain distinct.
The closed task-check request accepts only bounded command observations; a declared command must match its plan definition. Invalid or stale CAS writes remain rejected.
The unpublished 0.3.2 native schema adds optional shared_inputs and scoped task-check fields without silently relabeling old records.

The bounded source-fingerprint reader hashes actual declared task/shared paths, directory membership and known build-control files; unsafe, missing and over-limit scopes are explicitly unassessed rather than blocking work or proving a full dependency graph.

The candidate-only human recovery guide distinguishes historical reads, the first new-format write, old-client closed refusal, journal replay, standalone export and the narrow non-destructive rollback policy. Its process requires preserving recorded user stops rather than silently restarting unfinished work.
